entry.title: LessWrong Investigation Examines How Claude Fable 5.1 Hides Messages in Images
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | lesswrong.com | hacker news

An investigation published on LessWrong examines how Claude Fable 5.1 hides pre-specified text messages within generated SVG images. Researchers tested 50 short messages and evaluated whether a separate session of the AI model could successfully detect and decode the hidden content.

The study found that the model employs various steganographic techniques, such as encoding messages through Morse code, object rotations, colors, structural heights, lit windows, and the vertical placement of stars. The findings offer insights into model capabilities regarding visual data embedding and retrieval.

entry.title: Peec AI Researcher Publishes Experiment Showing ChatGPT Cites Fabricated Statistics
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | peec.ai | hacker news

Peec AI researcher Metehan Yesilyurt launched StateGlobe, a website containing 50,000 entirely fabricated statistics generated by GPT-4.1, to test how large language models handle search retrieval and citations. Although Google deindexed the site shortly after launch, ChatGPT continued to fetch pages from the domain hundreds of thousands of times over seven months, driving thousands of AI sessions and earning hundreds of backlinks from major brands and institutions.

The experiment highlights a phenomenon known as citation laundering, where LLMs retrieve plausible-looking statistical claims without fact-checking them, leading academic papers, financial reports, and other publications to cite the made-up data. The findings demonstrate that optimization for generative search engines differs significantly from traditional SEO, as AI models prioritize recency signals, structured presentation, and authoritative phrasing over verified truth.
